data.description:
## Summary

The MCP container image installs no `acli` (Atlassian CLI) binary, so every Jira-MUTATING bridge
operation on the deployed box fails at the transport with `[Errno 2] No such file or directory:
'acli'`. The Jira credentials are now correctly wired and authenticate; the binary that would use
them is absent.

## How it was found

Discovered while verifying `colourless-hasteless-lamb`, whose fix wired `JIRA_URL`, `JIRA_USER`,
`JIRA_PROJECT` and `JIRA_API_TOKEN` into the container. That fix moved `bridge_check_access` past
its credential gate and, in doing so, EXPOSED this defect — it was previously masked, because the
probe fail-closed on `missing_credentials` before ever reaching the transport.

## Observed (live, deployed container `rebar-mcp-25ea12c200ae-8092`, one run)

    rebar.bridge_check_access()
    {
      "steps": [
        {
          "step": "STEP_CREATE",
          "passed": false,
          "reason": "exception",
          "detail": "[Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'acli'"
        }
      ],
      "verdict": "FAIL"
    }

It fails at the FIRST step, `STEP_CREATE`, so `issue_key` stays `None`, the `finally` cleanup is a
no-op and nothing is left behind in Jira. Independently confirmed: a JQL census of
`project = REB AND summary ~ "rebar capability probe"` returned 0 before and 0 after.

## Established by inspection

- `infra/compose/Dockerfile.mcp` installs `git`, `openssh-client`, `ca-certificates`, `uv`, and the
  rebar package (`uv sync --locked --no-dev --extra agents --extra mcp --extra bedrock`). There is
  no `acli` install step.
- `grep -rn "acli\|atlassian" infra/compose/Dockerfile.*` returns NOTHING — no image in the compose
  stack provisions it, not just the mcp one.
- The dependency is real and load-bearing: `applier._load_acli()` resolves the transport, and
  `_backend.py:218` documents the CRUD transport against the remote tracker as
  "today: `acli.AcliClient`".

## Scope of the impact

The credentials themselves are proven good, so this is narrower than "Jira is broken":

- Jira-MUTATING paths are DEAD on the box: `bridge_check_access`, and `reconcile` in
  `bootstrap-strict` / `bootstrap-throttle` / `live`.
- Direct-REST paths still work. Verified live from inside the same container: authenticated
  `GET /rest/api/3/myself` -> 200 and `GET /rest/api/3/project/REB` -> 200, and a JQL search via
  `POST /rest/api/3/search/jql` returned 12 real REB issues.

So the failure is specifically the `acli` subprocess transport, not connectivity, not the
credentials, and not the project scope.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The mcp container image provisions an `acli` binary on `PATH`, pinned to an explicit version
      (no floating "latest"), with its provenance recorded the way the other pinned tools in the
      image are.
- [ ] A test asserts the image declares the `acli` install, so its removal cannot regress silently.
- [ ] `bridge_check_access` run in the deployed container reaches a verdict WITHOUT a
      `No such file or directory: 'acli'` exception at `STEP_CREATE`.
- [ ] If `acli` is deliberately NOT to be installed, that decision is recorded instead, together
      with what the bridge transport should be on the box, and the tools that depend on it report a
      typed "transport unavailable" verdict rather than surfacing a raw `FileNotFoundError` detail.
- [ ] No credential value is logged, printed, or committed by the fix or its verification.
data.title: MCP container image installs no acli binary, so every Jira-mutating bridge operation fails at the transport
